chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Touring with Maria Muldaur and Benny Carter
summary: Collins toured East Coast cities in Carter's band accompanying Muldaur, who sounded to him like a young Mildred Bailey.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And after that I went to New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore -- not Baltimore, Boston, and Washington with Benny, accompanying a singer, Marie Muldas. In the band was Harry Edison Addison, Marty Harris playing piano, John Williams playing bass, Earl --

-- Palmer drums, Plas Johnson, saxophone. And Frank Assolino, Snooky Young. But I don't think that Maria Muldar realized what -- how good the band was, you know. So consequently we got the write ups. The people, the critics would come to see her and we would get the write ups. If -- they loved her, but, you know, the band-- we had a couple of featured numbers, and that was it. You know. But she's so sweet she enjoyed it all and it just knocked her out. But I think that if she had known she would have given the band billing, you know.

But any way, I want to say this about Maria Muldar. The one thing that impressed me, the first time I heard her sing -- as a matter of fact we did an album with her. This -- so we did this tour as a result of the album. But the one thing that impressed me about Maria Muldar, she sounded like Mildred Bailey. And I asked her had she ever heard Mildred at this time and she said, no, but several people had told her this. But she sounded like, just like Mildred Bailey, a young Mildred Bailey.

So, you know, she -- I took her right to my heart there, as soon as I heard that. I think she was special to all of us then, you know, and she felt it. But we had a very successful tour with Lady Muldar.
